Class OpponentReader

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.OpponentReader
public final class OpponentReader extends Object
The opponent reader: what kind of opponent this is, read off the last three seconds of the fight. A window of a few numbers a tick (how far off the opponent is, how it moves, its sword and the fighter's own, the hits either way, and how far the opponent's last hit sent it) goes through a small network into sixteen numbers, and from those to a guess at the kind of opponent. The guess is learned the plain supervised way: in training the kind of every fight is known (what the critic is told, Trainer.episodeTask), and the reader is taught to name it. The sixteen numbers are what the tactics model (TacticNet) and the acting network (ActorNet) are handed, both through weights that start at zero; neither one's learning reaches back into the reader.

Why: the acting network sees one moment, and the three running averages of the opponent's style (ObsSpec.SC_STYLE_AWAY and the two after it) are all it had of the seconds before; it had learned to make next to no use of those. Against the jump-crit chaser, the whiffer and the 0.14.0 model it lost on 21 October what it won against the spacer and the timer: one way of fighting for all of them. Telling them apart is the first step to fighting each its own way. From a review the user passed on (21 October evening): an opponent encoder trained on the opponent's kind, its output not trained by the policy's gradient (as in auxiliary-task agents such as UNREAL, Jaderberg et al. ICLR 2017, and in policies that infer the opponent: He et al., DRON, ICML 2016), squashed with tanh so that its scale cannot drift. A window instead of a recurrent network: the networks here are written by hand, and a window needs no backpropagation through time.
